import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 9

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/9](https://www.erdosproblems.com/9)
-/

namespace Erdos9

/--
The set of odd numbers that cannot be expressed as a prime plus two powers of 2.
-/
def Erdos9A : Set ℕ := { n | Odd n ∧ ¬ ∃ (p k l : ℕ), (Nat.Prime p) ∧ n = p + 2 ^ k + 2 ^ l }


@[category test, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos9A_contains_one : 1 ∈ Erdos9A := by
  constructor
  · decide
  · push Not
    intro p k l hp
    linarith [Nat.Prime.two_le hp, @Nat.one_le_two_pow k, @Nat.one_le_two_pow l]

@[category test, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos9A_contains_three : 3 ∈ Erdos9A := by
  constructor
  · decide
  · push Not
    intro p k l hp
    linarith [Nat.Prime.two_le hp, @Nat.one_le_two_pow k, @Nat.one_le_two_pow l]

@[category test, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos9A_not_contains_five : 5 ∉ Erdos9A := by
  unfold Erdos9A
  simp only [exists_and_left, not_exists, not_and, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, not_forall, Decidable.not_not]
  intro
  use 3, Nat.prime_three, 0, 0
  simp only [pow_zero, Nat.reduceAdd]


/--
The set is known to be infinite. In [Er77c] Erdős credits Schinzel with proving that there are
infinitely many odd integers not of this form, but gives no reference.

[Er77c] Erdős, P., _Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III._.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_9.variants.infinite : Erdos9A.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
Is the upper density of the set of odd numbers that cannot be expressed as a prime plus
two powers of 2 positive?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_9 : answer(sorry) ↔ 0 < Erdos9A.upperDensity := by
  sorry

end Erdos9

review.notes:
Checked all six declarations. The source explicitly specifies odd integers n ≥ 1, a prime p, and exponents k,l ≥ 0, without requiring distinct powers. Erdos9A matches this exactly: Odd n over ℕ already implies n ≥ 1. The three membership tests are correct.

Lean experiments in /workspace/review/boundary.lean prove an executable bounded-search characterization of membership and verify that the exceptional numbers below 100 are exactly 1 and 3. The density checks confirm that upperDensity is the real-valued limsup of #(A ∩ [0,N))/N. These intersections are finite, the proportions lie in [0,1], and the zero denominator at N=0 is harmless. Answer polarity was also checked.

The current source records the density question as open and infinitude as established, agreeing with both research tags. Its revision history corroborates the historical Schinzel wording. Direct verification of that wording in Er77c was limited by an incorrect archive link and a publisher preview containing only the first two pages; the mathematical infinitude claim is independently explicit in the current cited source. No repository files were edited.
